description: Track A of the upstream-security process: automated monitoring of the
148 composer-visible packages in app/composer.lock.
This is JSON rather than JSON5 so the stdlib can parse it and the
fresh-clone gate can assert it is valid. Renovate ignores `description`
fields at every level, which is where the reasoning below lives.
STATUS: configured, not yet proven. There is no Renovate app installed on
this repository yet; enabling it is a forge decision (the same open
question as Wave 1.7's mirror). Expect the first run to need attention —
see `composer` below for the reason it may fail outright.
automergeDescription: Never. Auto-merge is wrong here specifically: merging is what triggers
the patch re-application this whole process exists to guard. 19 patches
are re-applied on every install, three of them against MediaWiki core and
two on the authentication path, and `scripts/verify-patches.sh
--upgrade-report` is a human step. A merge nobody looked at is a patch
enabledManagersDescription: Renovate would happily also bump the pinned images in .gitlab-ci.yml,
scripts/check.sh and the Dockerfiles. Those pins decide what CI's own
verdict is: ruff 0.15 -> 0.16 turned this repo's lint stage red with no
commit to blame (see ruff.toml), and opensearch/python/mariadb are
declared in VERSIONS.yml and gated by the version-consistency job. They
stay a human decision made in one place, not a PR from a bot.

description: app/composer.json is upstream's `bluespice/core`, so most versions here
are not this fork's to choose — a real fix usually means re-vendoring
the upstream tree (docs/dev/upgrade-runbook.md), not editing a range.
The value of these PRs is therefore the NOTIFICATION more than the diff.
Known failure mode on first run: hallowelt/chatbot and
mediawiki/page-header resolve from git@gitlab.hallowelt.com, which
Renovate cannot reach. docker/setup.sh strips both from composer.lock at
install time; Renovate has no such step, so lockfile resolution may fail
until they are excluded here or a host rule is added. They are ignored
below because updating them is impossible by definition — see Track C in
VERSIONS.yml and SECURITY.md.
One PR per upstream, not 148 PRs. bluespice/* moves as a release
train — 58 packages at one version — so splitting it into individual
PRs would produce a merge order that cannot be satisfied.

packageRules.description: Same reasoning for the MediaWiki extension packages.

description: Everything else grouped by update type, so a week of patch releases
arrives as one PR to review rather than twenty.
Security updates jump the schedule. This is the one case where
waiting for Monday is wrong, and it is the event the whole of §10
is designed around.
Complements scripts/ci/composer-audit.sh rather than duplicating it.
The gate answers 'has anything NEW appeared' on every push, offline
against a recorded baseline; this opens the PR that carries the fix.
